findings.summary: Page 1 tells the reader to set `merge.conflictStyle zdiff3` and names the `|||||||` base section six pages before conflict markers are introduced, and drops it inside the unrelated Range Syntax section.
findings.evidence: Page 1, immediately after the `5. Range Syntax` table: `"git config merge.conflictStyle zdiff3", "# adds the ||||||| base section", "# set --global; never guess intent again"`. The markers themselves are first shown on page 7: `"||||||| merged ancestor   # diff3 only"`.
findings.fix: Delete this code block from page 1 and place it on page 7 next to `2. Marker Anatomy`, where `<<<<<<<`, `=======` and `|||||||` are actually explained.

findings.summary: The rebase section's opening heading and code sit at the bottom of page 3 but its explanatory bullets are pushed to page 4 behind two leftover three-way-merge blocks, so the bullets arrive unlabelled after unrelated material.
findings.evidence: Page 3 ends with `{"type":"heading","text":"1. What It Computes"}` + `git rebase main   # replays main..feature`; page 4 then opens `"7. Strategy Options"` (-X ours / -s ours table) and the `"Cost Model"` callout before the bullets `"Take the commits in `main..feature`" / "Re-apply each in order on top of main"`.
findings.fix: Move the `7. Strategy Options` table and the `Cost Model` callout to the end of page 3 (they belong to three-way merge), and keep `1. What It Computes` + its code + its bullets together as the first block group of page 4.

findings.summary: Cherry-pick commands and the sentence explaining why cherry-picks conflict close page 4, one page before cherry-pick is defined and before the BASE/OURS/THEIRS mapping that the sentence refers to.
findings.evidence: Page 4 ends with `"git cherry-pick 9f2a1c      # one commit", "git cherry-pick main~4..main~1  # a range", "git cherry-pick -n a1b2     # stage only"` followed by `"That is exactly why a cherry-pick can conflict — it is never a blind patch application."`, while page 5 only then gives `"1. Rebase's Atom"` and the `"2. It Is A Three-Way Merge"` table (BASE = C's parent, OURS = HEAD, THEIRS = C).
findings.fix: Move the cherry-pick code block and that paragraph onto page 5, placing the code under `1. Rebase's Atom` and the paragraph directly after the `2. It Is A Three-Way Merge` table it is justifying.

findings.summary: The .gitattributes snippet uses `merge=ours`, which is not a built-in merge driver and silently falls back to the normal 3-way merge unless a driver is defined in git config.
findings.evidence: "# .gitattributes", "*.lock            merge=ours", "package-lock.json merge=ours" — gitattributes(5) lists only `text`, `binary` and `union` as built-in merge drivers; "The definition of a merge driver is done in the .git/config file, not in the gitattributes file".
findings.fix: Add the required driver definition alongside the attributes, e.g. show `git config merge.ours.driver true` (or `[merge "ours"] driver = true` in config) in the same snippet, and note that without it the attribute has no effect.

findings.summary: Page 8 prescribes `--force-with-lease --force-if-includes` as the closing command while the meaning and ranking of those flags are not given until page 9.
findings.evidence: Page 8 final block: `"git push --force-with-lease \\", "  --force-if-includes origin feature", "# 2.30+; error instead of silent overwrite"`; page 9 then introduces `"2. Force Flags Ranked"` with rows `["--force","none at all"],["--force-with-lease","remote tip = last fetched"],["--force-if-includes","lease survives a bg fetch"]`.
findings.fix: Move this code block to page 9, directly beneath the `2. Force Flags Ranked` table and its bullets, so the command follows the explanation of each guard.

findings.summary: Section numbers restart, duplicate, and run out of order on the same page across the part, making the numbered structure look broken.
findings.evidence: Page 9 shows both "4. Long Branches Lose" and "4. Branches With Merges", and both "5. Make It Mechanical" and "5. Where Rebase Is Fine"; page 4 shows "7. Strategy Options" and "7. Rebasing Your Pull"; page 3 shows "1. When It Is Needed" and "1. What It Computes"; page 5 opens at "8. Cost & Recovery" before "1. Rebase's Atom".
findings.fix: Renumber section headings per rendered page so each page runs 1..n with no repeats, or drop the leading numbers from headings entirely.

findings.summary: Page 2 closes with a paragraph defending three-way merge whose subject ("this") has no antecedent on a page about fast-forward, where BASE is by definition never consulted.
findings.evidence: Page 2 final block: `"Two-way diff cannot do this: without BASE, 'they added a line' and 'we deleted a line' look identical. BASE supplies intent."` — page 2 states earlier `"No merge base needed; conflict is impossible"`.
findings.fix: Move this paragraph to page 3, placing it immediately after the `2. The Three Inputs` table where BASE/OURS/THEIRS are named.

findings.summary: In a merge context the page tells readers to tune rename detection with `-M`, which is a diff/log option that `git merge` does not accept.
findings.evidence: "Default threshold 50%; tune with -M (e.g. -M40%)" in section "6. Renames Are Inferred" on the three-way-merge/ort page; merge-strategies(7) exposes rename tuning only as `-Xfind-renames[=<n>]` (with `rename-threshold=<n>` as a deprecated synonym) and `-Xno-renames`.
findings.fix: Rewrite as "Default threshold 50%; tune with `-X find-renames=40%` on merge/rebase (`-M40%` is the diff/log equivalent)."

findings.summary: The rebase identity bullet says the replayed commit has the "same tree", which is false whenever the new base contains any change — it is the patch that is preserved, not the tree.
findings.evidence: "Same tree, different parent, therefore different hash" under "2. New SHAs, Always"; a rebased commit's tree is the three-way merge result of new-base + the commit's diff, so it differs from the original tree unless the new base is content-identical to the old one.
findings.fix: Reword to "Same patch, new parent and usually a new tree, therefore a different hash" (matching page 2's "even if the diff is byte-identical").

findings.summary: A patch-id consequence is filed as the last bullet of the revert section, where it does not follow from anything around it.
findings.evidence: Page 5, `"7. Revert: The Inverse"` bullets: `"Applies the reverse diff as a NEW commit", "Adds history instead of rewriting it", "Therefore safe on shared branches", "Re-rebasing a merged branch is usually a no-op"`.
findings.fix: Move `"Re-rebasing a merged branch is usually a no-op"` into the `5. Patch-ID` bullets, right after `"Rebase drops picks whose patch-id is upstream"`, which is its actual premise.

findings.summary: The conflict-marker diagram labels the `|||||||` base section "diff3 only", contradicting page 1 and the Git docs, since zdiff3 also emits it.
findings.evidence: Page 7: "||||||| merged ancestor   # diff3 only" versus page 1: "git config merge.conflictStyle zdiff3 / # adds the ||||||| base section". git-merge docs: zdiff3 "is similar to diff3 but removes matching lines..." and its example shows `||||||| base:sample.txt`.
findings.fix: Change the comment to "# diff3 / zdiff3 only".

findings.summary: The page opens with a headless bullet list continued from the previous page, so the first block has no heading above it.
findings.evidence: Page 7 begins directly with "· A conflicted path holds 3 entries, not 1 / · Staging the path collapses it back to stage 0 / · That is the entire operation" under the "Page 7 : Conflicts: Anatomy & Fixes" banner, with the next heading being "2. Marker Anatomy"; page 9 has the same pattern above "4. Long Branches Lose".
findings.fix: Keep each section's heading with its bullets when paginating (avoid splitting a section across a page break), or repeat the heading as a "(cont.)" title at the top of the continuation page.

findings.summary: The conflicts page ends with a merge-vs-rebase equivalence claim whose "both" refers to two things never named on that page.
findings.evidence: Page 7 final block: `"With no conflicts both give the same tree. The entire difference is recorded history, not shipped code."`, on a page whose sections are index stages, markers, tree conflicts and `.gitattributes`.
findings.fix: Move this paragraph to page 8 and name the subjects, e.g. place it under the `1. Head-To-Head` tables whose last row already reads `["final tree","identical","identical"]`.

findings.summary: "Merge driver" is used as a gotcha on page 3 and then demonstrated on page 7 without ever being defined or connected to the `.gitattributes` syntax shown.
findings.evidence: Page 3 callout: `"it also runs no merge driver and creates no merge commit"`; page 7 `"8. Generated Files"` shows only `"*.lock            merge=ours", "package-lock.json merge=ours", "*.png             binary"` with no accompanying text.
findings.fix: Add a one-line lead-in to page 7 section 8 defining a merge driver (a per-path merge program selected via `.gitattributes`, e.g. `merge=ours` always keeps the current branch's version of a generated file) so the page-3 gotcha and this config resolve to the same concept.
